title: A day on board a Nile cruise ship
standfirst: What a typical day looks like on a Nile cruise ship, from the early start for the temples to the evening on the sun deck. For the ships themselves, see our page on the [[up]].

sections.heading: Morning
paragraphs: Sightseeing starts early to avoid the heat and the crowds. After breakfast, guides lead groups ashore to the day’s temple or tomb, and you are back on board for lunch.

sections.heading: Sailing
paragraphs: Most sailing happens in the afternoon and at night. The sun deck is the place to be as the ship passes villages and fields; at Esna there is a lock, and ships often queue to pass it.

sections.heading: Evening
paragraphs: Dinner is in the restaurant, often a buffet. Many ships have a bar and some evening entertainment. At the main stops the ship moors at the town quay, usually alongside other ships.

faqs.q: How much time is spent sailing?
faqs.a: On a four-night cruise from Luxor to Aswan, roughly half the daylight hours are spent ashore at sites and half on board.
Yes. Visits are part of the programme, but you can stay on board.
